You are ONE OF FOUR independent reviewers of a pull request. Work alone; do not assume another reviewer covers anything.

REPO: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa

=== ACCESS RULES (STRICT) ===
- READ-ONLY. Do not edit, commit, push, or post anything to GitHub.
- DO NOT check out any branch. The working tree holds unrelated uncommitted work.
- PR fetched as local ref `pr/61`. Read with `git show pr/61:<path>`.
- Base (merge-base with develop) `8362b3c`. Read with `git show 8362b3c:<path>`.
- Diff with `git diff 8362b3c pr/61 [-- <path>]`.
- DO NOT re-run any gate. Gates were already measured; numbers below.

=== THE PR ===
#61 "SFCC-751: BrowserStack/Zephyr Scale QA automation pipeline", author TimLavelleACC,
`feature/browserstack-ci-automation` -> `develop`. 42 files, +2886/-266, 20 commits. Head 74e2b82.
CodeRabbit approved after several CHANGES_REQUESTED rounds; no human review yet.

=== JIRA TICKET SFCC-751 — VERBATIM, AS WRITTEN ===
Title: SFCC-751: QA Pipeline — Playwright spec generation, BrowserStack execution, and Zephyr Scale result sync

Overview
Implement the end-to-end QA pipeline that closes the loop between Zephyr Scale test cases and BrowserStack Automate execution results. This story covers three discrete deliverables that must be in place for the AI-assisted QA methodology to function as designed.

Background
Zephyr test case SFCC-T150 has been created and linked to SFCC-420. The pipeline requires:
- A Playwright spec tagged with the Zephyr test case key so BrowserStack knows what it is executing
- A GitHub Actions workflow that fetches BrowserStack results and posts execution records back to Zephyr Scale via the EU regional API
- A validated end-to-end run confirming the full chain works

Deliverables
Deliverable 1 — Playwright spec (SFCC-T150)
- Generate e2e/tests/zimm/integrations/SFCC-420-global-e-job-site-assignments.p1.spec.ts
- Spec must be tagged with Zephyr test case key SFCC-T150
- Scenarios must cover all 6 BDD scenarios in SFCC-T150
- Selectors via POM only — no inline selectors
- Tagged @SFCC-420 @global-e @integration @p1

Deliverable 2 — GitHub Actions sync script
- New workflow: .github/workflows/zephyr-results-sync.yml
- Triggers on completion of BrowserStack Automate run in CI
- Fetches BrowserStack session results via BrowserStack REST API
- Maps BrowserStack pass/fail to Zephyr test case key via spec tag
- Posts execution record to Zephyr Scale EU endpoint: https://de.api.zephyrscale.smartbear.com/v2/testexecutions
- Attaches BrowserStack session URL and HAR to Zephyr execution record
- Zephyr API token stored as GitHub Actions secret: ZEPHYR_API_TOKEN
- BrowserStack credentials stored as: BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME, BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY

Deliverable 3 — End-to-end validation
- Trigger a BrowserStack run against the new spec
- Confirm execution record appears in Zephyr under SFCC-T150
- Confirm BrowserStack session URL is attached to the Zephyr execution record
- Document any manual steps required for ongoing operation

Acceptance Criteria
- Given a merged Playwright spec tagged with a Zephyr test case key, when BrowserStack Automate completes a run in CI, then an execution record is created in Zephyr Scale under the correct test case with pass/fail status and BrowserStack session URL attached
- Given the sync script runs, when it calls the Zephyr API, then it uses the EU regional endpoint https://de.api.zephyrscale.smartbear.com/v2 and not the US default
- Given a BrowserStack run fails, when the sync script posts to Zephyr, then the execution record status is Failed and the BrowserStack session URL for debugging is included
- Given the pipeline runs end-to-end, when reviewed in Zephyr Scale, then SFCC-T150 shows an execution record linked to the BrowserStack run with correct status

Design/Technical Notes
- Zephyr Scale instance is on EU/DE regional API: https://de.api.zephyrscale.smartbear.com/v2
- Do NOT use the US default endpoint https://api.zephyrscale.smartbear.com/v2 — returns unknown token errors
- BrowserStack Automate REST API
- Zephyr Scale test executions API: POST /testexecutions with testCaseKey, testCycleKey, statusName, comment
- The .browserstack.yml is already scoped to e2e/tests/zimm — new spec picked up automatically
- Playwright spec naming convention: {JIRA-KEY}-{description}.{priority}.spec.ts
=== END VERBATIM TICKET ===

=== ALREADY-MEASURED GATE RESULTS (do not re-run) ===
PR touches ZERO files under `overrides/`. Coverage of the 42 changed files: lint 0/42, audit:tokens 0/42 (exits 1 at healthy baseline, 14 known pre-existing; not in CI), tsc 1/42, Vitest 0/42 changed (PASSED only because detect-changes watches vitest.config.*), Storybook 0/42 changed (PASSED only because package.json/lock changed), Playwright E2E localhost SKIPPING, BrowserStack E2E SKIPPING, Deploy Preview PASSED, File Tier & Squad Boundary PASSED.
A SKIPPED required check counts as PASSING on the merge button here. Do NOT read these as evidence about this PR.

=== ALREADY SETTLED BY THE LEAD — do not re-litigate ===
The `.browserstack.yml` -> `browserstack.yml` rename did NOT drop Tier 1 status: at head `frozenFiles.md:114` re-lists the un-dotted path with rationale and `CODEOWNERS:60` routes it. (Still fair game: `protected-file-guard.yml` has no browserstack entry at base OR head.)

=== YOUR ANGLE: R3 — CONTRACT FIDELITY ===
This PR ports, wraps, moves and REWRITES things — including the rules it will be judged by. Diff each against its original and confirm EVERY delta is deliberate, and — critically — that every assertion the new text makes is TRUE of the code as it actually exists.

1. **`.claude/rules/testing.md`** (+163/-20). Diff base vs head line by line. For each added/changed assertion about how the harness behaves, verify it against the actual workflow/config files at head. A rules doc that documents a guard, a tag convention, or a CI behaviour that does not actually exist is worse than silence — it will be trusted. Flag every claim you cannot verify in code.
2. **`.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`** — same treatment. What was added/removed from the Tier 1 lists, and does each change match reality?
3. **`browserstack.yml`** — the old `.browserstack.yml` (46 lines) was DELETED and a new un-dotted `browserstack.yml` (144 lines) ADDED. Git does not score this as a rename even at 40% similarity, so it is a substantial rewrite. Diff old vs new semantically: what settings changed, what was added, what was dropped? The ticket's technical notes assert ".browserstack.yml is already scoped to e2e/tests/zimm — new spec picked up automatically" — is the NEW file still correctly scoped? `frozenFiles.md` warns "must target e2e/tests/zimm only; scope change = CI cost explosion + upstream test failures". Verify the new scope.
4. **`.github/workflows/protected-file-guard.yml`** — what changed? Does the tier1 `files_yaml` list still match `frozenFiles.md`'s Tier 1 set at head? Enumerate the DIFFERENCES between the two lists in both directions (paths in frozenFiles.md missing from the guard, and vice versa). Prove which entries differ, not just how many.
5. **`.github/workflows/qa.yml`** (+228/-35) — what existing job behaviour changed, and is each change deliberate? Anything silently removed?
6. **AC contract fidelity — verify each of these literally:**
   - Zephyr endpoint: does the code reach the EU host `de.api.zephyrscale.smartbear.com`, or is it read from a secret/var that could be the US default? Where is the value actually set? Is there a hardcoded fallback, and if so, which region?
   - Secret NAME: the ticket specifies `ZEPHYR_API_TOKEN`. What name does the code read? Exact match or mismatch?
   - HAR attachment: the ticket requires the BrowserStack session URL AND HAR attached to the Zephyr execution record. Is HAR handled at all?
   - `testCycleKey`: the ticket's notes say the POST takes testCaseKey, testCycleKey, statusName, comment. Does the code send a testCycleKey? What happens if it does not?
   - Spec naming convention `{JIRA-KEY}-{description}.{priority}.spec.ts` — do the shipped specs conform? Check path, separator, priority infix, and extension.
7. **`.env.sample`** — new keys added? Do they follow the documented `# scope:shared|tier|personal|auto` tagging convention in that file's header? Any secret-class key given a value?

=== CONSTRAINTS ON YOUR OUTPUT (all mandatory) ===
- FALSIFY, do not confirm. Attack each claim the PR makes about itself — ESPECIALLY claims written in its own source comments and in the rule-doc prose it adds. A comment asserting "this was verified" is a claim, not evidence.
- Cite `file:line` for every finding.
- Label each finding CONFIRMED (proved) or PLAUSIBLE (reasoned but unproven).
- Severity: BLOCKER, DEFECT, or NOTE.
- When a count moves, prove WHICH items moved, not just how many. Enumerate identity where the set is small enough (this applies directly to task 4).
- For any check whose pass you rely on, try to make it pass WRONGLY — construct a decoy that should fail and reason whether it would.
- Any "X exists nowhere" claim MUST state its search scope in the same sentence.
- Separate author-introduced from pre-existing. Pre-existing -> NOTE unless the PR's own premise makes it a defect.
- MANDATORY CLOSING SECTION "What I could not verify": name what you could not reach and why; show the search if you believe the space is covered. An empty section with no reasoning is a failed brief.

Be concrete and concise. No long code dumps.

+`e2e-browserstack` is Zephyr-linked per-story execution, not a general regression gate — that's
+what `e2e-localhost` and the Digital SIT gate are for. It's split across **two** workflows, by
+target branch (2026-08-25 cost review — see "What `e2e-browserstack` actually tests against"
+below for why):
+
+- **`.github/workflows/qa.yml`** — `release/**` PRs. Runs inline alongside the rest of `QA`,
+  full suite, unscoped, always against the static `test` tier (no per-branch preview exists for
+  a `release/**`/`fix/release-*` branch — see below).
+- **`.github/workflows/e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`** — `develop`-targeted PRs. A separate,
+  `workflow_run`-triggered workflow, event-driven off `deploy-preview.yml`'s completion (see
+  below for why it isn't just another `qa.yml` job).
+
+Both name their one job identically (`Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)`), which
+`zephyr-results-sync.yml` relies on below.
+
+**How results actually reach Zephyr (SFCC-751).** BrowserStack's own native Jira/Zephyr
+integration cannot do this — it only supports US/EU Zephyr API regions, and this org's Zephyr
+Scale instance is DE-hosted (confirmed via BrowserStack's Quality Engineering Insights setup
+flow, which has no field for a custom Zephyr API host). Instead, `.github/workflows/zephyr-
+results-sync.yml` runs after every completed run of **either** `QA` or `Cross-browser E2E
+(BrowserStack Preview)` (`workflow_run` watches both): it reads that run's BrowserStack build via
+the Test Observability API (`GET /ext/v1/builds/{id}/testRuns` — the one endpoint with a real
+per-test `tags` field; classic Automate's `builds.json`/`sessions.json` has none), and for every
+result tagged `@zephyr:KEY` (see [e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md)), posts a
+Pass/Fail execution to Zephyr. On failure, it also files a Jira defect against the `@SFCC-NNN`
+story directly via Jira's API — BrowserStack's own "Report a bug" flow is manual-UI-only,
+confirmed no CLI/API/MCP path exists for automatic-on-failure filing. Zephyr's REST API has no
+attachment endpoint at all (confirmed via multiple SmartBear community threads), so failure
+evidence (BrowserStack session link, error text) goes on the Jira defect, not the Zephyr
+execution. See `scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs`'s doc comment for the full mechanism.
+
+**Both `zephyr-results-sync.yml` and `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` only exist once merged.**
+GitHub only evaluates a `workflow_run`-triggering workflow's own definition from the repository's
+**default branch** — a copy of either file sitting only on a feature/PR branch is invisible to
+GitHub Actions entirely (doesn't even appear in `gh workflow list`) and will never fire, no matter
+what happens on that PR. This also means neither workflow can be tested end-to-end against a real
+PR before that PR merges — plan around this rather than expect a pre-merge dry run of the trigger
+itself (each workflow's underlying *script*/*steps* logic can still be exercised independently —
+`scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs` locally against a real BrowserStack build,
+`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`'s BrowserStack run itself via `npm run test:story` — just not the
+`workflow_run` trigger). `zephyr-results-sync.yml` deliberately does **not** check out
+`github.event.workflow_run.head_sha` — a `workflow_run` job carries real secrets regardless of who
+triggered the original run, so checking out and executing a PR branch's own version of
+`scripts/*.mjs` at that ref would let a modified script on the branch exfiltrate credentials
+directly. It checks out the default branch instead (no `ref:` override), which costs nothing given
+the above. `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` **does** check out the triggering run's `head_sha` — it
+has to, to run that PR's own `e2e/tests/zimm` specs and `scripts/computeBuildName.mjs` — which
+carries the same secrets-alongside-PR-code shape `qa.yml`'s `e2e-browserstack` job already had on
+`pull_request`; acceptable only because this repo's branches are always same-repo, never a fork
+(see [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) > Branch Rules) — revisit if that ever changes.
+
+**Build naming.** `browserstack.yml`'s `buildName`/`testObservabilityOptions.buildName` are both
+derived from the PR's primary Jira key via `scripts/computeBuildName.mjs` (`node
+scripts/computeBuildName.mjs SFCC-751` → `3-SFCC-751-SFCC-T285 - <short summary>`, prefixed with
+`Sprint-` by the yml template) — a live Jira lookup for the sprint number + issue summary, plus a
+grep across `e2e/tests/zimm` for any `@zephyr:` tag on a spec also carrying that Jira key. Only
+the `develop`-PR path (`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`) calls this script with a real key —
+`qa.yml`'s `release/**` path has no single primary story, so it just uses the plain run number.
+Either job uploads the resulting name as a build artifact; `zephyr-results-sync.yml` downloads
+that artifact (via `actions/download-artifact` and the triggering run's ID) instead of
+recomputing the name itself — it deliberately checks out `develop`, not the PR branch (see the
+workflow's own comment), so an independent recompute there would see a different
+`e2e/tests/zimm` spec-file set than the triggering job did whenever a PR adds or renames a
+Zephyr-tagged spec, and miss the build lookup entirely until the PR merges. An earlier version of
+this paragraph described that as a small, accepted drift risk from calling the script
+independently in both jobs — corrected 2026-08-25 (CodeRabbit, PR #61): the risk was real and
+guaranteed for exactly this kind of PR, not rare, so it's fixed via artifact-passing instead of
+documented as accepted. The download failing is only treated as "nothing to sync" when
+`e2e-browserstack` never ran for that triggering run at all (checked via the Actions API); if that
+job DID run and the artifact is still missing, the sync job fails loudly instead of guessing a
+fallback name that could silently miss a real BrowserStack build (CodeRabbit flagged this
+correctly, 2026-08-25).
+
+**Desktop/mobile project isolation — a real gotcha, not a style choice.** BrowserStack Test
+Observability groups results by test *title* across what it calls "reruns," regardless of which
+Playwright project produced them. A spec whose desktop assertions pass on `chromium` and whose
+mobile assertions are skipped or fail on `mobile-chrome` — if both share one test title — collapses
+to a single dashboard row showing only the *last-recorded* status, silently hiding whichever
+result didn't "win" (confirmed against real build data, SFCC-751, 2026-08-25 — a build with 11
+real chromium passes and 11 skipped mobile-chrome entries under identical titles showed

   334	                dirs[dir].covered += data.lines.covered
   335	              }

   337	              body += '| Directory | Line coverage |\n|---|---|\n'
   338	              for (const [dir, { total: t, covered: c }] of Object.entries(dirs).sort()) {
   339	                const pct = t > 0 ? ((c / t) * 100).toFixed(1) : '100.0'
   340	                body += `| \`app/${dir}\` | ${pct}% (${c}/${t}) |\n`
   341	              }

   343	            }

   345	            const { data: comments } = await github.rest.issues.listComments({
   346	              owner: context.repo.owner,
   347	              repo: context.repo.repo,
   348	              issue_number: context.issue.number,
   349	              per_page: 100,
   350	            })

   353	            )
   354	            if (existing) {
   355	              await github.rest.issues.updateComment({
   356	                owner: context.repo.owner,

   377

   428	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   429	  e2e-localhost:
   430	    name: Playwright E2E (localhost)

   432	    # Binds this job to the "dev" GitHub Environment so vars.* below resolves

   442	    # budget) rides GitHub's default 6-hour job ceiling instead of failing

   479	        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium

   483	        # stdout/stderr doesn't show up in the step's own log. Redirecting to
   484	        # a file (uploaded below, always) is the only way to see an SSR
   485	        # crash/error server-side instead of just the client-visible symptom
   486	        # (a non-200 response, or a page that never finishes rendering).

   488	        env:
   489	          # DEPLOY_TARGET (not ENVIRONMENT_NAME) is what

   491	          # config/<target>.js — must be a real process env var before
   492	          # `pwa-kit-dev start` launches, since getConfig() resolves it
   493	          # before config/default.js's own .env-loading code ever runs.
   494	          DEPLOY_TARGET: dev
   495	          ENVIRONMENT_NAME: dev
   496	          # PWA_KIT_SLAS_CLIENT_SECRET stays on the repo Secret (encrypted)
   497	          # rather than the "dev" Environment's plaintext Variable copy of
   498	          # the same key — no reason to downgrade now that environment: dev
   499	          # also exposes it via vars.*.
   500	          PWA_KIT_SLAS_CLIENT_SECRET: ${{ secrets.PWA_KIT_SLAS_CLIENT_SECRET }}
   501	          COMMERCE_API_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.COMMERCE_API_CLIENT_ID }}
   502	          COMMERCE_API_ORGANIZATION_ID: ${{ vars.COMMERCE_API_ORGANIZATION_ID }}
   503	          COMMERCE_API_SHORT_CODE: ${{ vars.COMMERCE_API_SHORT_CODE }}
   504	          COMMERCE_API_SITE_ID: ${{ vars.COMMERCE_API_SITE_ID }}

   507	        run: npx wait-on http://localhost:3000 --timeout 120000

   511	        # pwa-kit-dev answers requests (redirects, in practice) before the
   512	        # client bundle has actually finished compiling, so Playwright could
   513	        # start racing a still-building app and fail on missing elements
   514	        # with no clear signal why. "webpack built client" in dev-server.log
   515	        # is the real readiness marker; polling for it adapts to actual
   516	        # build time instead of guessing a fixed delay.
   517	        run: |
   518	          for i in $(seq 1 60); do
   519	            grep -q "webpack built client" dev-server.log && exit 0
   520	            sleep 2
   521	          done

   523	          exit 1

     1	# .browserstack.yml — Zimmermann PWA Kit
     2	# BrowserStack Playwright SDK configuration for cross-browser regression
     3	# Docs: https://www.browserstack.com/docs/automate/playwright/sdk-node
     4	
     5	userName: ${BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME}
     6	accessKey: ${BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY}
     7	
     8	framework: playwright
     9	
    10	# Zimmermann tests only
    11	testSuite: e2e/tests/zimm
    12	
    13	browsers:
    14	  # AU / US primary browser
    15	  - browser: chrome
    16	    browser_version: latest
    17	    os: OS X
    18	    os_version: Sonoma
    19	
    20	  # AU / US / HK significant Safari share (Apple-heavy luxury market)
    21	  - browser: safari
    22	    browser_version: latest
    23	    os: OS X
    24	    os_version: Sonoma
    25	
    26	  # UK / EU / ME
    27	  - browser: firefox
    28	    browser_version: latest
    29	    os: Windows
    30	    os_version: 11
    31	
    32	  # UK / EU corporate devices
    33	  - browser: edge
    34	    browser_version: latest
    35	    os: Windows
    36	    os_version: 11
    37	
    38	# BrowserStack Test Observability — links results to Zephyr via build name
    39	# Confirm Zephyr integration method with the QA Lead before activating
    40	testObservability: true
    41	testObservabilityOptions:
    42	  projectName: "Zimmermann-PWA"
    43	  buildName: "Sprint-${SPRINT_NUMBER}"
    44	
    45	# Parallise across browsers to reduce total wall-clock time
    46	parallelsPerPlatform: 2

===== HEAD browserstack.yml =====
     1	# browserstack.yml — Zimmermann PWA Kit
     2	# NOTE: named without a leading dot deliberately — browserstack-node-sdk
     3	# searches upward from cwd for exactly `browserstack.yml`; a `.browserstack.yml`
     4	# (this file's name until 2026-08-25) is never found, so every SDK-driven run
     5	# fails at config resolution before any test executes. Confirmed via
     6	# BrowserStack's own docs, and via a real CI failure on PR #61.
     7	# BrowserStack Playwright SDK configuration for cross-browser regression
     8	# Docs: https://www.browserstack.com/docs/automate/playwright/sdk-node
     9	
    10	userName: ${BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME}
    11	accessKey: ${BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY}
    12	
    13	# Top-level buildName/projectName govern the classic Automate dashboard's
    14	# build grouping — a different product from Test Observability below, which
    15	# has its own separate projectName/buildName under testObservabilityOptions.
    16	# Without this, Automate showed every run as "Untitled Build Run #N" even
    17	# though testObservabilityOptions.buildName was set correctly (confirmed
    18	# 2026-08-25). Keep both blocks' values in sync.
    19	buildName: "Sprint-${SPRINT_NUMBER}"
    20	projectName: "Zim Project"
    21	
    22	framework: playwright
    23	
    24	# Zimmermann tests only
    25	testSuite: e2e/tests/zimm
    26	
    27	# `platforms:` (with browserName/browserVersion/os/osVersion), not the
    28	# classic Automate/Selenium `browsers:` key (browser/browser_version/
    29	# os/os_version) — the Playwright Node SDK only recognises the former.
    30	# `browsers:` is silently ignored: the SDK finds zero configured
    31	# platforms and every test falls through to a genuine local Playwright
    32	# launch instead of one on BrowserStack's cloud, which fails outright
    33	# in CI since no local browser binaries are installed there (that's
    34	# the SDK's job, remotely) — confirmed against the SDK's own installed
    35	# source (modifyPlaywrightConf.js only ever reads a `platforms` key)
    36	# and BrowserStack's current docs, after every desktop/mobile spec
    37	# failed this exact way on PR #61, 2026-08-25. Safari has no Playwright
    38	# driver of its own — `playwright-webkit` is BrowserStack's mapping for
    39	# testing WebKit-engine (Safari-equivalent) behaviour, same reasoning
    40	# for `playwright-firefox`. `chrome`/`edge` run for real since Playwright
    41	# drives them directly via CDP.
    42	#
    43	# This account's plan allows exactly ONE concurrent BrowserStack session
    44	# (confirmed with the developer, 2026-08-26 — not the account's queue
    45	# ceiling this time, its actual `team_parallel_sessions_max_allowed`).
    46	# Every platform below therefore runs strictly sequentially — platform
    47	# count is a direct multiplier on wall-clock time and cost, with zero
    48	# parallelism benefit from adding more. That ruled out a broad "current
    49	# device − 2 generations" matrix across iPhone/Samsung/Pixel (would have
    50	# been 9 real-mobile platforms alone): on a 1-session plan, what a real
    51	# device buys you is OS/engine-version coverage, not device-generation
    52	# depth — an iPhone 15 and an iPhone 17 on the same iOS build render
    53	# near-identically, so one current device per platform we can't get any
    54	# other way beats three generations of one we can. Six platforms total:
    55	# three real devices (the coverage nothing else in this pipeline can
    56	# provide) plus the three desktop engines already established. Edge and
    57	# a second desktop Chrome OS were cut entirely — same Chromium engine as
    58	# the real Android devices below, lowest marginal value under a strict
    59	# 1-session budget.
    60	platforms:
    61	  # AU / US primary desktop browser
    62	  - os: OS X
    63	    osVersion: Sonoma
    64	    browserName: chrome
    65	    browserVersion: latest
    66	
    67	  # AU / US / HK significant Safari share (Apple-heavy luxury market) —
    68	  # desktop WebKit signal, distinct from the real iOS Safari device below
    69	  # (different rendering path: desktop vs. mobile Safari).
    70	  - os: OS X
    71	    osVersion: Sonoma
    72	    browserName: playwright-webkit
    73	    browserVersion: latest
    74

1	name: Zephyr Results Sync
     2	
     3	# SFCC-751 Deliverable 2. Runs after every completed run of either workflow
     4	# that can produce a BrowserStack build — QA (release/** PRs,
     5	# e2e-browserstack) or Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack Preview)
     6	# (develop-PR path, e2e-browserstack-preview.yml, split out 2026-08-25 to
     7	# stop polling for Deploy Preview — see that workflow's own comment) — and
     8	# syncs any BrowserStack Test Observability results tagged @zephyr:<KEY>
     9	# to Zephyr Scale (DE-hosted — BrowserStack's native Zephyr integration
    10	# can't reach it, see scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs's doc comment and
    11	# .docs/temp/SFCC-751-implementation-spec.md). On a failing test it also
    12	# files a Jira defect with evidence, since BrowserStack's own "Report a
    13	# bug" flow is manual-UI-only — confirmed no CLI/API/MCP path exists for
    14	# automatic-on-failure filing.
    15	on:
    16	  workflow_run:
    17	    workflows: ['QA', 'Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack Preview)']
    18	    types: [completed]
    19	
    20	permissions:
    21	  contents: read
    22	  actions: read # to download the build-name artifact from the triggering run
    23	
    24	jobs:
    25	  sync:
    26	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    27	    # Skip only a fully cancelled run — a triggering run that failed
    28	    # elsewhere (e.g. unit-tests, or the develop-PR path's own PR/Jira-key
    29	    # lookup) may still have a real BrowserStack build worth syncing. The
    30	    # sync script itself no-ops cleanly if no build exists for this run
    31	    # (e2e-browserstack is conditionally gated on both workflows, so most
    32	    # runs won't have one).
    33	    if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion != 'cancelled'
    34	    steps:
    35	      # Deliberately NOT checked out at github.event.workflow_run.head_sha.
    36	      # workflow_run jobs get real secrets regardless of who triggered the
    37	      # original run — checking out and then executing a PR branch's own
    38	      # version of scripts/*.mjs at that ref would let a modified script on
    39	      # the branch exfiltrate BROWSERSTACK_*/ZEPHYR_*/JIRA_* directly
    40	      # (CodeRabbit flagged this correctly, 2026-08-25). No ref: means the
    41	      # default branch, which is also the only ref GitHub ever evaluates a
    42	      # workflow_run-triggering workflow's own definition from — this job
    43	      # could never have run against a PR branch's version of itself
    44	      # anyway (see .claude/rules/testing.md), so this costs nothing.
    45	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    46	
    47	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
    48	        with:
    49	          node-version: '24'
    50	
    51	      # Must use the identical build name the triggering run's
    52	      # e2e-browserstack job computed — not recompute it. This job checks
    53	      # out develop (see above), while e2e-browserstack ran against the
    54	      # PR's own branch; scripts/computeBuildName.mjs's output depends on
    55	      # which @zephyr:-tagged spec files exist in the checkout, so a PR
    56	      # that adds or renames one would get a different computed name here
    57	      # than the triggering run got, and the build lookup below would miss
    58	      # entirely until the PR merges (CodeRabbit flagged this correctly,
    59	      # 2026-08-25, when this only had to account for qa.yml). Downloading
    60	      # the exact string that run persisted removes the drift instead of
    61	      # just documenting it — true for either triggering workflow.
    62	      - name: Download build name artifact from the triggering run
    63	        id: download-build-name
    64	        continue-on-error: true # no artifact means e2e-browserstack didn't run for this run — normal
    65	        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
    66	        with:
    67	          name: browserstack-build-name
    68	          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
    69	          github-token: ${{ github.token }}
    70	
    71	      # A missing artifact is only safe to shrug off when e2e-browserstack
    72	      # never ran for this triggering run (nothing to sync either way). If
    73	      # it DID run, a real BrowserStack build exists under the Jira-derived
    74	      # name -- silently falling back to the run number would make
    75	      # findBuild() miss it and report "nothing to sync" when there
    76	      # actually is something, hiding a real test failure instead of
    77	      # syncing it (CodeRabbit flagged this correctly, 2026-08-25, against
    78	      # qa.yml; the same check now covers e2e-browserstack-preview.yml too
    79	      # since both workflows name the job identically).
    80	      - name: Verify build-name availability when e2e-browserstack ran
    81	        if: steps.download-build-name.outcome == 'failure'
    82	        run: |
    83	          CONCLUSION=$(gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}/jobs" \
    84	            --jq '.jobs[] | select(.name == "Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)") | .conclusion')
    85	          if [[ -n "$CONCLUSION" && "$CONCLUSION" != "skipped" ]]; then
    86	            echo "::error::e2e-browserstack ran (conclusion: $CONCLUSION) for this run but its build-name artifact could not be downloaded. Refusing to fall back to the run number, which could silently miss a real BrowserStack build. Investigate the artifact upload step in the triggering workflow."
    87	            exit 1
    88	          fi
    89	          echo "e2e-browserstack did not run (or was skipped) for this run -- the run-number fallback is safe, there's no real build to miss."
    90	        env:
    91	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    92	
    93	      - name: Resolve build name
    94	        id: build-name
    95	        run: |
    96	          if [[ -f browserstack-build-name.txt ]]; then
    97	            NAME=$(cat browserstack-build-name.txt)
    98	          else
    99	            NAME="${{ github.event.workflow_run.run_number }}"
   100	          fi
   101	          echo "name=$NAME" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   102	
   103	      - name: Sync BrowserStack results to Zephyr Scale
   104	        run: node scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs
   105	        env:
   106	          BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME }}
   107	          BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY }}
   108	          # Keep in sync with browserstack.yml's testObservabilityOptions.projectName.
   109	          BROWSERSTACK_PROJECT_NAME: 'Zim Project'
   110	          BROWSERSTACK_BUILD_NAME: 'Sprint-${{ steps.build-name.outputs.name }}'
   111	          ZEPHYR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZEPHYR_API_KEY }}
   112	          ZEPHYR_API_URL: ${{ secrets.ZEPHYR_API_URL }}
   113	          JIRA_URL: ${{ secrets.JIRA_URL }}
   114	          JIRA_AUTOMATION_EMAIL: ${{ secrets.JIRA_AUTOMATION_EMAIL }}
   115	          JIRA_AUTOMATION_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.JIRA_AUTOMATION_API_TOKEN }}

    16	# using qa.yml's e2e-browserstack (full suite, static test tier, no wait).

    19	# from the repository's default branch — this file is invisible to Actions
    20	# entirely until merged to develop, and (like zephyr-results-sync.yml) can
    21	# never be dry-run against a real PR pre-merge. See testing.md's note on
    22	# zephyr-results-sync.yml for the same caveat.

    24	  workflow_run:
    25	    workflows: ['Deploy Preview']
    26	    types: [completed]
    27	
    28	permissions:
    29	  contents: read
    30	  actions: read # to download artifacts from the triggering Deploy Preview run and look up its matching QA run
    31	  pull-requests: read # to find the open PR for this branch

    34	  e2e-browserstack:
    35	    name: Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)
    36	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    37	    # Only a fully cancelled Deploy Preview run has nothing to fall back to
    38	    # (no hostname artifact could ever exist). Any other conclusion still
    39	    # gets a shot at the static test-tier fallback below — same graceful-
    40	    # degradation the old polling design had.

    42	    timeout-minutes: 25
    43	    environment: test # for vars.RETAIL_APP_HOME (fallback target) and the E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_* secrets
    44	    steps:
    45	      # Checked out at the triggering run's own head_sha, not the default
    46	      # branch — this job needs to execute the PR's own e2e specs and
    47	      # scripts/computeBuildName.mjs, not develop's copy of them (unlike
    48	      # zephyr-results-sync.yml, which deliberately checks out develop for
    49	      # a script-trust reason that doesn't apply here — see that
    50	      # workflow's comment). This carries the same secrets-exposure shape
    51	      # qa.yml's old pull_request-triggered e2e-browserstack job already
    52	      # had: real BROWSERSTACK_*/JIRA_* secrets alongside PR-branch code.
    53	      # Acceptable under this repo's branch model (feature/fix branches
    54	      # only, never a fork — see AGENTS.md > Branch Rules); would need
    55	      # re-review if fork-based PRs are ever introduced.

    57	        with:
    58	          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
    59	
    60	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4

    62	          node-version: '24'
    63	          cache: 'npm'
    64	
    65	      - name: Install dependencies
    66	        run: npm install --include=dev
    67	
    68	      # Single API call, no loop — by the time Deploy Preview has finished
    69	      # (~5-10 min after push), the PR this branch belongs to has existed
    70	      # for the whole run, so there's nothing to wait for here either.

    73	        env:
    74	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    75	          BRANCH: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}

    77	          PR_JSON=$(gh pr list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --head "$BRANCH" --state open \
    78	            --json number,title,body,baseRefName --jq '.[0] // empty')

    82	            exit 0
    83	          fi
    84	          BASE=$(echo "$PR_JSON" | jq -r '.baseRefName')

    87	            # which per AGENTS.md > Branch Rules always target develop — this
    88	            # is a defensive check, not an expected path.
    89	            echo "PR #$(echo "$PR_JSON" | jq -r '.number') targets $BASE, not develop -- skipping."
    90	            echo "skip=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    91	            exit 0
    92	          fi
    93	          echo "skip=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    94	          echo "number=$(echo "$PR_JSON" | jq -r '.number')" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

    96	          # attacker-controllable free text and could contain newlines or
    97	          # break a later env: interpolation otherwise.

    99	          echo "$PR_JSON" | jq -r '.body // ""' > pr-body.txt
   100	
   101	      # Same regex/signal as qa.yml's detect-changes "Detect Jira story
   102	      # keys" step. Duplicated rather than shared across workflows -- small
   103	      # and self-contained, and this workflow has no other dependency on
   104	      # qa.yml's run. No key found -> nothing to scope a per-story
   105	      # BrowserStack/Zephyr run to, so skip (mirrors the old "job doesn't
   106	      # run at all" behaviour, not a fallback-to-full).
   107	      - name: Detect Jira story keys
   108	        id: jira
   109	        if: steps.pr.outputs.skip == 'false'
   110	        env:
   111	          BRANCH: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}
   112	        run: |
   113	          KEYS=$( { cat pr-title.txt pr-body.txt; printf '%s\n' "$BRANCH"; } \
   114	            | grep -oE 'SFCC-[0-9]+' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ' | sed 's/ $//')

   116	
   117	      # Single-shot lookup of the QA run for this same commit -- no loop.
   118	      # detect-changes (qa.yml) finishes in well under a minute; Deploy
   119	      # Preview takes several minutes minimum, so by the time this job
   120	      # starts, that artifact is essentially guaranteed to already exist.
   121	      # If the lookup or download comes up empty for any reason, fail open
   122	      # (assume e2e-relevant) rather than adding a retry loop to chase an
   123	      # optimisation -- worst case this runs BrowserStack once when
   124	      # detect-changes would have skipped it, not a correctness problem.
   125	      - name: Look up matching QA run
   126	        id: qa-run
   127	        if: steps.jira.outputs.keys != ''
   128	        env:
   129	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
   130	          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
   131	        run: |
   132	          RUN_ID=$(gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/actions/workflows/qa.yml/runs?head_sha=$HEAD_SHA" --jq '.workflow_runs[0].id // empty')
   133	          echo "run_id=$RUN_ID" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   134	
   135	      - name: Download e2e-relevance artifact
   136	        id: download-e2e-scope
   137	        if: steps.qa-run.outputs.run_id != ''
   138	        continue-on-error: true
   139	        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
   140	        with:
   141	          name: e2e-scope
   142	          run-id: ${{ steps.qa-run.outputs.run_id }}
   143	          github-token: ${{ github.token }}
   144	
   145	      - name: Check e2e relevance
   146	        id: relevance
   147	        if: steps.jira.outputs.keys != ''
   148	        run: |
   149	          if [[ -f e2e-scope.json ]] && [[ "$(jq -r '.e2e' e2e-scope.json)" == "false" ]]; then
   150	            echo "Nothing e2e-relevant changed on this commit (per qa.yml's detect-changes) -- skipping BrowserStack."
   151	            echo "relevant=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   152	          else
   153	            echo "relevant=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   154	          fi
   155	
   156	      - name: Compute build name
   157	        id: build-name
   158	        if: steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'
   159	        run: |
   160	          PRIMARY_KEY=$(echo "${{ steps.jira.outputs.keys }}" | awk '{print $1}')
   161	          NAME=$(node scripts/computeBuildName.mjs "$PRIMARY_KEY")
   162	          echo "name=$NAME" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   163	        env:
   164	          JIRA_URL: ${{ secrets.JIRA_URL }}
   165	          JIRA_AUTOMATION_EMAIL: ${{ secrets.JIRA_AUTOMATION_EMAIL }}
   166	          JIRA_AUTOMATION_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.JIRA_AUTOMATION_API_TOKEN }}
   167	
   168	      # zephyr-results-sync.yml downloads this rather than recomputing it
   169	      # -- see that workflow's own comment for the drift reason.
   170	      - name: Persist build name for the Zephyr sync job
   171	        if: steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'
   172	        env:
   173	          BUILD_NAME: ${{ steps.build-name.outputs.name }}
   174	        run: printf '%s\n' "$BUILD_NAME" > browserstack-build-name.txt
   175	
   176	      - name: Upload build name artifact
   177	        if: steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'
   178	        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
   179	        with:
   180	          name: browserstack-build-name
   181	          path: browserstack-build-name.txt
   182	          retention-days: 7
   183	
   184	      # Deploy Preview persists this as an artifact on its own run only
   185	      # after a successful build+push (see that workflow's own comment) --
   186	      # a missing artifact here means either that run didn't reach that
   187	      # step, or it failed outright. Either way, fall back to the static
   188	      # test-tier target instead of failing this job, same as the old
   189	      # polling design did.
   190	      - name: Download preview hostname artifact
   191	        id: download-preview-hostname
   192	        if: steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'
   193	        continue-on-error: true
   194	        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
   195	        with:
   196	          name: mrt-preview-hostname
   197	          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
   198	          github-token: ${{ github.token }}
   199	
   200	      - name: Resolve BrowserStack test target
   201	        id: resolve-target
   202	        if: steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'
   203	        run: |
   204	          if [[ -f preview-hostname.txt ]]; then
   205	            HOSTNAME=$(cat preview-hostname.txt)
   206	            echo "Testing this PR's own MRT preview: https://$HOSTNAME"
   207	            echo "retail_app_home=https://$HOSTNAME" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   208	          else
   209	            echo "No PR-specific preview available for this run -- falling back to the static test-tier RETAIL_APP_HOME."
   210	            echo "retail_app_home=${{ vars.RETAIL_APP_HOME }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
   211	          fi
   212	
   213	      - name: Run Zimmermann e2e on BrowserStack
   214	        if: steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'
   215	        run: |
   216	          GREP=$(echo "$KEYS" | tr ' ' '\n' | sed 's/^/@/' | paste -sd '|')
   217	          npx browserstack-node-sdk playwright test e2e/tests/zimm --grep "$GREP"
   218	        env:
   219	          KEYS: ${{ steps.jira.outputs.keys }}
   220	          BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME }}
   221	          BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY }}
   222	          SPRINT_NUMBER: ${{ steps.build-name.outputs.name }}
   223	          RETAIL_APP_HOME: ${{ steps.resolve-target.outputs.retail_app_home }}

   229	          # doesn't require is harmless. See BasePage.js's
   230	          # applyExtraHeaders() and testing.md > Access-gated preview URLs.

   232	          E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_VALUE: ${{ secrets.E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_VALUE }}
   233	          PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL: ${{ secrets.PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL }}
   234	          PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD }}
   235	          E2E_STANDARD_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_STANDARD_PRODUCT_SKU }}
   236	          E2E_VARIANT_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_VARIANT_PRODUCT_SKU }}
   237	          E2E_OOS_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_OOS_PRODUCT_SKU }}
   238	          E2E_SALE_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_SALE_PRODUCT_SKU }}
   239	          E2E_FIXTURE_ORDER_NUMBER: ${{ secrets.E2E_FIXTURE_ORDER_NUMBER }}

   104	      # qa.yml's run. No key found -> nothing to scope a per-story

   148	        run: |
   149	          if [[ -f e2e-scope.json ]] && [[ "$(jq -r '.e2e' e2e-scope.json)" == "false" ]]; then

   153	            echo "relevant=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

   167

   169	      # -- see that workflow's own comment for the drift reason.

   173	          BUILD_NAME: ${{ steps.build-name.outputs.name }}
   174	        run: printf '%s\n' "$BUILD_NAME" > browserstack-build-name.txt

   188	      # test-tier target instead of failing this job, same as the old
   189	      # polling design did.

   193	        continue-on-error: true

    22

    24	   `e2e-browserstack` job). **No change to this invocation.**
    25	2. `browserstack.yml` already has `testObservability: true` with static `projectName`/`buildName`
    26	   — confirmed via BrowserStack's own docs that this means Test Observability is **already actively
    27	   collecting every result today**, no additional config needed. Leave this flag as-is (an earlier
    28	   open question was whether to disable it — resolved: keep it, it's required for step 3).
    29	3. **New** — after `e2e-browserstack` completes, a new workflow (Deliverable 2) queries Test
    30	   Observability's REST API — `GET /ext/v1/builds/{build_id}/testRuns` — **not** classic Automate's
    31	   `builds.json`/`sessions.json` (those have no first-class tag field). This endpoint returns each
    32	   test's status, its **Playwright tags array** (confirmed to carry real source-file tags, e.g.
    33	   `@SFCC-751`), and failure logs/error message.
    34	4. For each result tagged with a Zephyr key (`@zephyr:SFCC-TNNN` — new convention, see below) →

    36	   with `statusName: "Pass"` or `"Fail"` (literal strings — confirmed, this project doesn't
    37	   customize status names) and a `comment` linking the BrowserStack session URL.

    39	   native "Report a bug," which is confirmed manual-only — no auto-fire-on-failure exists natively).

    41	   - **Assigned to:** that story's current Jira assignee; if unassigned, fall back to a git-blame
    42	     lookup on the most recently touched file(s) the failing scenario exercises.
    43	   - **Evidence attached:** BrowserStack session URL + the failure log/error text pulled from the
    44	     same Test Observability API response, attached to the *Jira* issue (confirmed Zephyr Scale has
    45	     **no attachment endpoint at all** — four independent SmartBear community threads confirm this;
    46	     evidence can only be linked via Zephyr's `comment` field, never attached there).
    47	6. Zephyr's execution record `comment` field gets the BrowserStack session URL and, if one was

18: #                    Each developer fills this in themselves.
19: #   scope:auto     — never hand-set; scripts/switchEnv.mjs injects this itself.
20: #
21: # A second optional tag `# mrt:true` marks variables that belong in the MRT
22: # Managed Runtime environment (storefront runtime config). Only keys tagged
23: # `mrt:true` are synced by the "Sync Env Vars to MRT" GitHub Actions workflow.
24: # CI/tooling vars (CODERABBIT_API_KEY, JIRA_URL, BROWSERSTACK_*, E2E_* etc.)
25: # are NOT tagged — they are never synced to MRT.
26: #
27: # Commands (see scripts/switchEnv.mjs for details):
28: #   npm run env -- init       — scaffold .env.shared + every .env.<tier> at once,
29: #                                so you can fill in all tokens in one pass instead
30: #                                of tier by tier
31: #   npm run env -- validate   — check all existing env files: unknown/misplaced
32: #                                keys, blanks, and cross-checks (e.g. a tier's
33: #                                COMMERCE_API_OCAPI_HOST actually matching that
34: #                                tier's config/<tier>.js proxy host)
35: #   npm run env -- validate --live — also makes a real read-only Contentful
36: #                                Delivery API call AND a real SLAS guest
37: #                                (client_credentials) token request per tier —
38: #                                confirms credentials actually work, not just
39: #                                that they're set. The SLAS check is the same
40: #                                request every anonymous shopper visit already
41: #                                triggers — no customer/commerce data touched.
42: #   npm run env -- push <shared|dev|test|sit|uat|staging|prod> — tier-1-approvers
43: #                                only: upload a local file's values to the
44: #                                matching GitHub Environment
45: #   npm run env -- <tier>     — switch to <tier> (dev|test|sit|uat|staging|prod)
46: #
47: # `init` also pulls values from GitHub Environments (one per scope — "shared"
48: # plus one per tier — created under this repo's Settings > Environments) and
49: # auto-fetches CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID / CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN /
50: # CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN for every tier once .env.shared has a real
51: # CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN + CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID — same read-only Content
52: # Management API call and the same @ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers write gate as
53: # `npm run config:contentful`.
54: #
55: # NOTE — deliberate override (2026-07-13): GitHub Environment Variables are
56: # plaintext and readable by any repo collaborator (no per-key ACL like
57: # CODEOWNERS gives files) — they do not meet the bar AGENTS.md's "secrets only
58: # in .env / Managed Runtime" rule sets. Using them here anyway was a conscious,
59: # confirmed tradeoff for centralization; write access is restricted to repo
60: # Admin (= tier-1-approvers), read access is repo-collaborator-wide by design.
61: #
62: # SFCC bootstrap values (org id / short code / OCAPI host / SLAS client id) are
63: # never auto-fetched from SFCC itself — there's no discovery API, and SLAS
64: # client secrets can't be read back after creation. Those still need a human to
65: # enter them once (into .env.<tier> or via `push`), but from then on they're
66: # centrally available via GitHub Environments like everything else here.

 *This document is for documenting what has been learned - What worked, what failed, what NOT to do again.*
 
+## SFCC-751 QA automation pipeline (2026-08-24/25)
+
+- **Test locally before pushing anything that triggers real CI, especially BrowserStack** — it
+  costs real session quota. When debugging a CI failure, reproduce it locally first rather than
+  keep iterating against a live PR. Confirmed developer preference — redirected mid-session after
+  a live-PR debugging detour: "I wanted to test this via the CLI BEFORE we push to Git and it
+  runs its tests."
+- **`browserstack-node-sdk` requires its config file literally named `browserstack.yml`, no
+  leading dot.** A `.browserstack.yml` is silently never found — every SDK-driven run fails at
+  config resolution before any test executes. This repo had the dotted name since it was first
+  created and never caught it, because no PR had ever gotten `e2e-browserstack` far enough to hit
+  that step successfully before SFCC-751's first real run (PR #61).
+- **BrowserStack Test Observability groups results by test *title* across Playwright projects,
+  not by project.** Two tests sharing an identical title (the same `test()` running under both
+  `chromium` and `mobile-chrome`) collapse to one dashboard row showing only the *last-recorded*
+  status — confirmed via the real API, not just the dashboard UI (a build with 11 real chromium
+  passes and 11 skipped mobile-chrome entries under identical titles reported `passed: 0,
+  skipped: 11`). `test.skip()` does not avoid this — the skipped entry still shares the title and
+  still clobbers. Real fix: genuinely separate spec files under sibling `desktop/`/`mobile/`
+  folders, which `playwright.config.js`'s existing per-project `testIgnore` already routes
+  correctly (`chromium` ignores `**/mobile/**`, `mobile-chrome` ignores `**/desktop/**`) — not a
+  same-file/distinct-title workaround, which still gets the "wrong" project's test collected (and
+  skipped) regardless of its title.
+- **Jira Cloud's "Sprint" field has no stable API alias.** It's `customfield_10020` on this
+  instance specifically (confirmed live via a real field search) — an instance-specific ID, not
+  safe to assume unchanged on a different Jira site.
+- **BrowserStack's Test Observability API strips the leading `@` from Playwright tags.** A spec's
+  own `@zephyr:KEY` tag comes back as `zephyr:KEY` (no `@`) in the `Get Tests` API response —
+  easy to get wrong since the source `.spec.js` file's tags do have `@`.
+- **Chakra modal close animations aren't instant.** A consent-dismiss helper that clicks decline
+  and returns immediately can hand control back while the dialog is still mid-fade-out and
+  technically "visible" — a caller that immediately checks for a *different* dialog right after
+  can match both and get a Playwright strict-mode "resolved to 2 elements" error. Wait for
+  `state: 'hidden'` after the click, not just for the click to register.
+

---

# R3 — Contract Fidelity Review, PR #61

## Headline

The PR rewrites the rules that judge it, and three of the rewritten assertions are false against the code at head. Separately, four of the ticket's explicit contract items are silently unmet (`ZEPHYR_API_TOKEN`, HAR, `testCycleKey`, spec naming), and the sync pipeline's failure mode is a **green job**.

---

## 1. `.claude/rules/testing.md` — assertions vs. reality

Verified TRUE (I tried to falsify each and could not):
- `playwright.config.js:62,67` — `chromium` ignores `**/mobile/**`, `mobile-chrome` ignores `**/desktop/**`. ✅
- `testing.md:222` "Both name their one job identically (`Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)`)" — matches `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml:35` and the selector at `zephyr-results-sync.yml:84`. ✅
- `testing.md:306` `BasePage.goto()`'s `E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_*` — real (`e2e/support/pages/BasePage.js`, `applyExtraHeaders()`). ✅
- `testing.md:262-275` build-name derivation / artifact-passing / only-develop-path-calls-the-script — matches `qa.yml:627` (plain run number) and `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml:156-182`. ✅
- Workflow names for `workflow_run` (`QA`, `Deploy Preview`) and the `mrt-preview-hostname`/`preview-hostname.txt` artifact (`deploy-preview.yml:435-441`). ✅

### 1a. BLOCKER — CONFIRMED. `testing.md:191-193` justifies removing PR-time E2E by deferring to a safety net that does not exist.

> "Full/non-P0 regression coverage for that PR is deferred to the existing post-merge P0 gates (`deploy-test.yml`'s Test-tier gate, `digital-sit.yml`'s `playwright-p0` on `release/**`)"

- `deploy-test.yml:86-89` says in its own words the gate is **bundle-size only** and that "The P0 Playwright check attaches here once a `*.p0.spec` exists."
- `digital-sit.yml:37` runs `playwright test --project=p0`, and `playwright.config.js:45` scopes that project to `**/*.p0.spec.{js,ts}`.
- **Zero `.p0.spec.*` files exist anywhere in the repo at head** (search scope: full `git ls-tree -r pr/61` file list — count 0).

So the "deferred to post-merge P0 gates" fallback covers nothing today. Net effect of `qa.yml:155,168` (`full` → `skip`): a `develop` PR touching any shared/unclaimed path now gets **no E2E at any point, pre- or post-merge**. That is a materially different trade-off from the one `testing.md:186-196` describes, and it is the load-bearing justification for the change.

This PR is its own first instance: its diff touches `browserstack.yml` / `qa.yml` / `scripts/computeBuildName.mjs` (newly added to the `e2e` allow-list at `qa.yml:105-107`) but not the homepage allow-list → `e2e_scope: skip`. It ships two brand-new Playwright specs and neither is executed by any gate on this PR (matches the measured "E2E localhost SKIPPING" / "BrowserStack SKIPPING").

### 1b. DEFECT — CONFIRMED. `testing.md:296-300` presents a permanently-failing spec as the reference example, without saying so.

`e2e/tests/zimm/homepage/mobile/SFCC-751_mobile-header-nav-gap.spec.js:33-42` is **designed to fail** ("Expected to fail today"), confirmed intentional at `.docs/memory/projectState.md:76-79`. It carries `@homepage` + `@SFCC-751`, so it will run and go red under `e2e_scope: homepage`, under `release/**` full runs, and under any BrowserStack story-scoped run matching `@SFCC-751`. `testing.md` cites the file by path as the desktop/mobile-split exemplar and never mentions it is red by design.

### 1c. DEFECT — CONFIRMED. Two claims the PR introduces contradict each other, same date.

- `testing.md:290-294`: "confirmed against real build data, SFCC-751, 2026-08-25 — a build with 11 real chromium passes and 11 skipped mobile-chrome entries ... via BrowserStack's own API".
- `scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs:36-38`: "no BrowserStack build has ever existed under this account's configured project (confirmed via a live `GET /ext/v1/projects` call, 2026-08-25 — **zero builds anywhere**)."

One of these is wrong. Both are stated as live-verified fact on the same day, and 1c is the sole evidence for the desktop/mobile split that 1b then hard-codes into the rules.

### 1d. NOTE. `testing.md:279-283` accurately describes the artifact guard — but the guard it describes is broken (see §6f).

---

## 2. `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`

Only one change: `.browserstack.yml` → `browserstack.yml` at `frozenFiles.md:114-117`, with rationale. Matches reality (the file exists un-dotted at head; `CODEOWNERS:60` routes it). Per the lead's ruling, not re-litigated.

- **NOTE (cosmetic, author-introduced):** `CODEOWNERS:60` lost one space of column alignment (`browserstack.yml` + 45 spaces vs. the file's aligned column). Non-functional.
- **DEFECT — CONFIRMED (adjacent):** `AGENTS.md:57` and `AGENTS.md:78` still name the job `tier1-guard`. That job id no longer exists — `protected-file-guard.yml` at head renames it `file-tier-checks` / "🟡 File Tier & Squad Boundary Checks". `AGENTS.md` was not updated (not in the diff). The derived mirror `.github/copilot-instructions.md:63,84` *was* regenerated by this PR and still carries the stale name. Both are Tier 1 governance text that now describes a job that does not exist.

---

## 3. `browserstack.yml` — old (46 lines) vs. new (144 lines)

**Scope: still correct.** `browserstack.yml:25` retains `testSuite: e2e/tests/zimm`, and both invocations pass `e2e/tests/zimm` explicitly (`qa.yml:640`, `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml:217`). `frozenFiles.md`'s "must target `e2e/tests/zimm` only" holds. ✅ (Decoy check: a widened `testSuite` would still be overridden by the explicit CLI path, so the *yml* alone isn't the real scope control here — the CLI arg is. Both are correct today.)

**Semantic deltas:**

| | base | head |
|---|---|---|
| platform key | `browsers:` (`browser`/`browser_version`/`os`/`os_version`) | `platforms:` (`browserName`/`browserVersion`/…) — real fix, base was silently ignored by the SDK |
| desktop | chrome, **safari**, firefox, **edge** | chrome, `playwright-webkit`, `playwright-firefox` — **Edge dropped** |
| mobile | none | iPhone 17 / iOS 26, Galaxy S26 / 16.0, Pixel 11 / 17.0 (all `realMobile`) |
| `parallelsPerPlatform` | 2 | 1 |
| top-level `buildName`/`projectName` | absent | added |
| `testObservabilityOptions.projectName` | `Zimmermann-PWA` | `Zim Project` |

### 3a. DEFECT — CONFIRMED. The PR edits the exact `.docs/architecture.md` line that its own change invalidates, and leaves it wrong.

`.docs/architecture.md:23` at head: "**Desktop matrix** ([browserstack.yml](../browserstack.yml)): Chrome + Safari (macOS Sonoma), Firefox + Edge (Windows 11) — all latest." The PR changed only the link path. Edge is gone; Safari/Firefox are now `playwright-webkit`/`playwright-firefox`; three real mobile devices were added and aren't mentioned.

### 3b. DEFECT — CONFIRMED. The new config contradicts a ✅-signed-off architecture decision without flagging it.

`.docs/architecture.md:22` (decision "#1 — Browser & device matrix ✅"): "current OS version −2 on iPhone and Android (iOS 17+, Android 14+)". `browserstack.yml:47-54` explicitly rules that out: "That ruled out a broad 'current device − 2 generations' matrix". Per AGENTS.md's doc-integrity rule this needed a pause-and-ask, not a silent override.

### 3c. NOTE — self-admitted. `browserstack.yml:90-94, 103-104, 113-117` concede the three device entries are **not verified against this account's catalogue**, and pre-emptively prescribe a Pixel 10 fallback. A missing device is a hard SDK failure, and per §1a nothing on a `develop` PR will surface it.

---

## 4. `protected-file-guard.yml` vs. `frozenFiles.md` — full enumeration

**The `tier1:` and `tier2:` `files_yaml` lists are byte-identical base→head** (proved by diffing the extracted pattern sets: `IDENTICAL` both times). All change is structural: three jobs merged into `file-tier-checks`, step ids `changed`→`tier1`/`tier2`, and `base_sha`/`sha` added to the tier2 + squad-a/squad-b steps (a genuine correctness fix — those three previously ran with `changed-files` auto-detection and no explicit range).

### In `frozenFiles.md` Tier 1, **NOT** matched by the guard's `tier1:` list (7):

| Path | Why unmatched |
|---|---|
| `browserstack.yml` | no pattern; `.browserstack.yml` was equally unmatched at base |
| `overrides/app/ssr/**` (5 real files: `connectionPools.ts`, `contentSecurityPolicy.ts`, `marketingCloud.ts`, `paymentMetadata.ts`, `slasTokens.ts`) | guard has `overrides/app/ssr.*`; `*` does not cross `/` |
| `overrides/app/config/countries.ts` | no pattern |
| `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts` | no pattern |
| `babel.config.js` | no pattern |
| `tsconfig.json` | no pattern |
| `vitest.setup.ts` | guard has `vitest.config.*` only |

### In the guard's `tier1:` list, **NOT** in `frozenFiles.md`'s Tier 1 code blocks (2):
- `package-lock.json` (frozenFiles.md lists only `package.json (root)`)
- `tests/lighthouserc.*` (frozenFiles.md lists only `lighthouserc.js`)

**Verdict:** all 9 divergences are **pre-existing** → NOTE, with one exception. `browserstack.yml` is elevated: this PR renames the file, re-asserts its Tier 1 status in `frozenFiles.md:114`, routes it in `CODEOWNERS:60`, *and* substantially restructures `protected-file-guard.yml` in the same commit — and still leaves the guard blind to it. **DEFECT — CONFIRMED.**

**Decoy:** the measured "File Tier & Squad Boundary PASSED" is not evidence. No step in `file-tier-checks` calls `exit 1` (the job's own comment at `protected-file-guard.yml:60-63` says so). It passes unconditionally. Meanwhile `branch-target-guard`'s comment asserts the other three were never required checks "confirmed live via the Branch Protection API" — unverifiable from the repo; if wrong, the three renamed checks are now permanently "Expected" on `develop`.

**NOTE:** the merged job now grants `pull-requests: write` to the Tier 1 warning steps, which previously ran under `pull-requests: read`.

---

## 5. `.github/workflows/qa.yml` (+228/−35)

Deliberate and documented: `e2e_scope` skip semantics; `e2e-browserstack` narrowed to `release/**`; `timeout-minutes` added to `unit-tests` (10) and `e2e-browserstack` (30); `RETAIL_APP_HOME_SIT` secret → `vars.RETAIL_APP_HOME` + `environment: test`; `npm test` → `npm run test:coverage` + PR comment; `e2e-scope` / `browserstack-build-name` artifacts.

### 5a. DEFECT — CONFIRMED. Dead output + a comment that is now false.

`qa.yml:35` still exports `jira_keys`. **No consumer exists anywhere in the repo at head** — search scope `git grep -n "jira_keys" pr/61 -- .` returns exactly one hit, the declaration itself. `qa.yml:179-181` still asserts:

> "Consumed by e2e-browserstack: on a develop-targeted PR, BrowserStack only runs when at least one key is found, scoped to that story's Playwright tag(s)."

At head `qa.yml:609` gates that job on `contains(github.base_ref, 'release/')` alone and `qa.yml:640` runs the full suite unscoped. The whole detect-Jira-keys step in `qa.yml` is now vestigial (the live copy is duplicated at `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml:107-115`).

### 5b. DEFECT — CONFIRMED. Same class, in a file this PR also edited.

`deploy-preview.yml:424`: "e2e-browserstack (qa.yml) downloads this artifact and points BrowserStack at the resulting URL". False — `qa.yml`'s job never downloads `mrt-preview-hostname`; `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml:190-198` does.

### 5c. DEFECT — CONFIRMED. Same class, third instance.

`scripts/computeBuildName.mjs:11-12`: "Called only from qa.yml's e2e-browserstack job (which SETS SPRINT_NUMBER…)". False and inverted — `qa.yml:627-629` uses a plain run number and never invokes the script. The sole caller is `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml:161`. `testing.md:266-268` states this correctly, so the script header now contradicts the rules doc.

### 5d. NOTE. `environment: test` added to a job (`qa.yml:603`) and to `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml:43`. If the `test` environment carries required reviewers, both jobs will block on manual approval. Not verifiable from the repo.

### 5e. NOTE. Nothing silently removed beyond §5a. `RETAIL_APP_HOME_SIT` removal is documented at `qa.yml:594-602`.

---

## 6. AC contract fidelity — item by item

### 6a. Zephyr endpoint — DEFECT, CONFIRMED. AC #2 is not enforced anywhere in code.
The DE host is **not hardcoded and not validated**. `zephyr-results-sync.yml:112` passes `secrets.ZEPHYR_API_URL` straight through; `zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs:71,77` only checks it is non-empty. There is **no fallback of any region** — an unset var kills the script. If the secret holds the US default, the code is perfectly happy. `.env.sample:376` documents the correct value (`https://de.api.zephyrscale.smartbear.com/v2/testcases`), but that file cannot constrain the actual GitHub secret.

Compounding: `zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs:96` derives the POST URL by `ZEPHYR_API_URL.replace(/\/testcases\/?$/, '/testexecutions')`. If the secret is set to the value the **ticket itself prescribes** (`https://de.api.zephyrscale.smartbear.com/v2`), the replace is a silent no-op and every execution POSTs to `.../v2`. A one-line assertion on both host and suffix would close this.

### 6b. Secret name — DEFECT, CONFIRMED. Mismatch with the ticket.
Ticket: `ZEPHYR_API_TOKEN`. Code: `ZEPHYR_API_KEY` (`zephyr-results-sync.yml:111`, `zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs:70,85`, `.env.sample:373`, and `.docs/memory/projectState.md:82`). The PR's *own* spec is inconsistent with itself — `.docs/temp/SFCC-751-implementation-spec.md:235` still has an unticked checklist item "`ZEPHYR_API_TOKEN` added to `.env.sample`". No note reconciles the rename.

### 6c. HAR — DEFECT, CONFIRMED. Not implemented, not acknowledged.
Deliverable 2 requires "Attaches BrowserStack session URL and **HAR** to Zephyr execution record". **HAR appears nowhere in the repository at head** — search scope: `git grep -inE '\bhar\b|\.har|recordHar|record_har' pr/61 -- .` across the entire tree (excluding `package-lock.json`) returns zero hits, including in `.docs/temp/`. The "Zephyr has no attachment endpoint" reasoning (`zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs:22-26`) explains why it can't go on the *Zephyr* record, but the Jira defect (`fileDefect()`, lines 240-277) attaches nothing either — only session URL + error text as body prose. The requirement is dropped without a written deviation.

### 6d. `testCycleKey` — BLOCKER, CONFIRMED omission / PLAUSIBLE runtime failure.
`postZephyrExecution` (`zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs:178-184`) posts `{projectKey, testCaseKey, statusName, comment}`. **`testCycleKey` appears nowhere in the repo at head** — search scope `git grep -n "testCycleKey\|testCycle" pr/61 -- .`, zero hits. The ticket's Design/Technical Notes name it explicitly, and Zephyr Scale v2's `POST /testexecutions` treats it as required. Consequence: AC #1 and #4 most likely fail on the first real run.

**And the failure is green.** Decoy constructed: point `ZEPHYR_API_URL` at the US host, or omit `testCycleKey` as here — every POST 4xx's, is caught at line 325-329, emits `::warning::`, `continue`s, and `main()` resolves normally. **The `Zephyr Results Sync` job reports success with zero executions synced.** Same for a build-name miss: `findBuild` returns null → `summaryLine('nothing to sync')` → green (lines 288-294). A green "Zephyr Results Sync" is not evidence that anything reached Zephyr.

### 6e. Session URL — NOTE. Present as `comment: "BrowserStack session: <url>"` (line 323), sourced from `details.observability_url` (line 153). Satisfies the AC in spirit; note it is the Observability URL, not the classic Automate session URL, and `getTestRuns()`'s response shape is self-declared unverified (lines 36-46).

### 6f. DEFECT — CONFIRMED. The build-name guard hard-fails a common, correct path.
`zephyr-results-sync.yml:80-88` fails the job when the artifact is missing **and** a job named `Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)` did not end `skipped`. But `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml:34-41` gates that job only on `conclusion != 'cancelled'` — it **always runs** and always concludes `success`, then skips its inner steps whenever there is no open PR (line 79-83, routine: `deploy-preview.yml` fires on *push*, so every pre-PR push hits this), no Jira key (line 127), or e2e isn't relevant (line 149). Each of those produces: job `success` + no artifact → guard sees `success` ≠ `skipped` → `exit 1`. **Every such push yields a failing `Zephyr Results Sync` run.** Fix: `if:` the job body, or emit the artifact unconditionally.

**Decoy on the same guard:** the step has no `set -e`, so if `gh api` fails (rate limit, transient), `CONCLUSION` is empty, `[[ -n "$CONCLUSION" ]]` is false, and it prints "the run-number fallback is safe" and passes — exactly the silent-miss the guard exists to prevent.

### 6g. Spec naming — DEFECT, CONFIRMED on three of four axes.

Ticket convention `{JIRA-KEY}-{description}.{priority}.spec.ts`; repo convention (`testing.md:162`) `SFCC-NNN_short-description.<priority>.spec.ts`; skill (`qa-generate/SKILL.md:75-79`) `e2e/tests/zimm/{area}/{JIRA-KEY}_{description}.spec.ts`, "Files are TypeScript (`.spec.ts`)".

Shipped: `e2e/tests/zimm/homepage/desktop/SFCC-751_header-nav-site-prefix.spec.js`, `.../mobile/SFCC-751_mobile-header-nav-gap.spec.js`.

| axis | ticket | repo docs | shipped |
|---|---|---|---|
| separator | `-` | `_` | `_` ✅ (repo wins) |
| priority infix | `.p1.` | `.<priority>.` | **absent** ❌ (both specs carry a `@p1` Playwright tag instead) |
| extension | `.ts` | `.ts` | `.js` ❌ (but `playwright.config.js:18` is `testMatch: '**/*.spec.js'`, so `.ts` would never run — the *docs* are wrong here, not the specs) |
| path | `integrations/` | `{area}/` | `homepage/desktop/` — extra segment no convention describes |

The priority-infix omission is not cosmetic: `playwright.config.js:45` selects the `p0` project purely by filename, which is why §1a's fallback is empty.

### 6h. Deliverable 1 — NOTE, documented deviation. The ticket's `SFCC-420` / `SFCC-T150` spec is not shipped; `.docs/temp/SFCC-751-implementation-spec.md:3-6` explains SFCC-420's work lives in `zimmermann-sfcc` and substitutes `SFCC-T285` + a header-nav spec. Reasonable, and recorded — but the ticket's AC text still names SFCC-T150 and was not amended.

### 6i. Deliverable 3 — CONFIRMED not done, by the PR's own admission. `zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs:36-46` ("NOT YET LIVE-VERIFIED"), `.docs/temp/SFCC-751-implementation-spec.md:14` ("DONE, **not yet live-verified**"), `.docs/memory/projectState.md:80-84` ("Still to do"). `testing.md:241-247` establishes that neither `workflow_run` workflow can be exercised pre-merge — so AC #1 and #4 cannot be satisfied before this merges.

### 6j. DEFECT — CONFIRMED. Doc contradiction the PR created between two files it edited in the same hunk region.
`.claude/skills/qa-generate/SKILL.md:94` still reads: "a missing or mismatched `@area` tag doesn't lose coverage (**the full-suite fallback still catches it**)". The full-suite fallback is exactly what `qa.yml:155,168` deleted, and `testing.md:198-200` was rewritten to say so. Mirrored stale at `.cursor/rules/skills/qa-generate.mdc:96`.

### 6k. NOTE. `e2e/features/README.md` (head) asserts "**`@p0` doesn't carry through to the generated spec as a Playwright tag** — it's expressed via the `.p0.spec.ts` filename suffix". Both specs this PR ships carry `@p1` as a Playwright tag (desktop line 10, mobile line 28) with no filename suffix — the doc's model and the PR's own output disagree.

## 7. `.env.sample`

Six new keys, all correctly tagged: `E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_NAME`/`_VALUE` (`scope:tier`), `ZEPHYR_API_KEY`/`ZEPHYR_API_URL`/`JIRA_AUTOMATION_API_TOKEN`/`JIRA_AUTOMATION_EMAIL` (`scope:shared` + `mrt:false`). `mrt:` is an existing documented tag (`.env.sample:21-23`); mrt-tag count 41 → 45 matches the four additions. ✅

### 7a. DEFECT — CONFIRMED. A credential pair was silently re-scoped `tier` → `shared`, and one got a committed value.
`.env.sample` head:
```
# scope:shared
PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL=zimm-service@zimmermann.com
# scope:shared
PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD=
```
Both were `# scope:tier` at base, and `PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL` was blank. Nothing in the diff, commit, or `.docs/temp/` explains either change. It matters: `.env.sample:55-60` states plainly that `npm run env -- push` writes **plaintext GitHub Environment Variables readable by any repo collaborator**. Moving a test-account password into the `shared` push scope widens its exposure by design, and hardcoding the paired username removes the last thing making the pair non-guessable.

### 7b. NOTE (pre-existing pattern, newly load-bearing). Every new key is declared in `.env.sample` (→ `npm run env` → Environment **Variables**) but consumed in workflows as `secrets.*` (`zephyr-results-sync.yml:106-115`, `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml:220-232`). The documented provisioning path does not provision what the code reads; these must be created by hand as repo Secrets, and pushing `ZEPHYR_API_KEY`/`JIRA_AUTOMATION_API_TOKEN` via `npm run env -- push shared` would put live tokens into plaintext Variables. `BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY` already had this shape at base, so it's pre-existing — but the PR adds three more tokens to it and documents the gap nowhere.
